metadata.scenario_context: Emily has finally been accepted into college, and her family is planning a celebration for her academic achievement.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Peru strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying lilies as a gift for Emily.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily's academic achievement party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, I was thinking... what if we get some lilies for Emily's celebration? They’re beautiful and symbolize purity and renewal, which seems fitting for her starting college. What do you think? 

Also, I wonder, do you really believe one of your main goals in life should be to make your parents proud? I sometimes feel like that's not *my* goal at all.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I think lilies are a nice idea... they really do symbolize something special. But... what about getting her a book or something related to her major? It feels more personal for a college celebration. 

As for making my parents proud, well, it's really important to me. They’ve sacrificed a lot for me. I want to honor that... it's part of my identity, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, I get that a book could be personal, but I still think lilies add a nice touch. They're classic and can be a beautiful centerpiece for the celebration.

But about making your parents proud... I just don’t see it that way. Sometimes I think we should focus more on our own paths rather than just trying to uphold expectations. It feels like... a lot of pressure, you know?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I don’t really see meaningful differences here. Everyone has their own way of looking at things, and that's fine. At the end of the day, it's all the same. People figure it out in their own time. 

But back to the gift... I still think a book could be great for Emily. It's practical and thoughtful. Lilies are nice, but maybe we should focus on something she can use in her college journey, you know?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
